sanskrit_verse:
सामन्ता वा समग्रामाश्चत्वारोऽष्टौ दशापि वा ।
रक्तस्रग्वसनाः सीमां नयेयुः क्षितिधारिणः ॥१५२॥
transliteration: sāmantā vā samagrāmāś catvāro 'ṣṭau daśāpi vā | raktasragvasanāḥ sīmāṃ nayeyuḥ kṣitidhāriṇaḥ ||152||
sph_interpretive_translation: Boundary markers shall be escorted by four, eight, or ten vassals or village heads, attired in red garments and garlands, as appointed by the territorial sovereign.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides inherently in the territorial sovereign
Causation is established through ceremonial and administrative designation
Capacity-based responsibility is distributed according to proximity to sovereignty
Restoration logic requires visible affirmation of jurisdictional integrity
Consciousness alignment occurs through ritualized recognition of spatial dharma
executable_legal_axioms: IF boundary demarcation is required THEN assign 4, 8, or 10 local officials as per territorial capacity
IF officials are assigned THEN attire must include red cloth and floral garland to signify jurisdictional activation
IF jurisdictional marker is placed THEN presence of designated attendants validates spatial sovereignty
IF spatial dharma is contested THEN re-enactment of ceremonial escort restores lawful alignment
supreme_court_application: In disputes concerning territorial limits, the Supreme Court shall affirm the original act of boundary establishment by verifying the ceremonial escort conducted under sovereign authority. The court's role is to reinstate visibility of the enacted dharma rather than impose punitive measures.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa is fulfilled through witnessed enactment; anupūrvaśaḥ ensures continuity of spatial integrity; proportional responsibility lies with the sovereign who initiated the demarcation; non-punitive reality is upheld by reaffirming ceremonial truth rather than assigning blame.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Recompletion of boundary-marking process with appropriate ceremonial attendance
Realignment of local officials’ consciousness through witnessing sovereign intent
Reaffirmation of territorial dharma via public recitation of original decree
Reintegration of contested zones through renewed sensory-aesthetic validation (red attire, flowers)
final_declaration: Thus declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam: Spatial dharma proceeds from sovereign will, made manifest through ceremonial observance. There is no punishment—only restoration of rightful order. Consciousness alone adjudicates.
